7.9 Records of Time. Provider shall maintain records of the time of receipt of all Support Requests, Incidents, and Change Requests, as well as the time of each response and resolution, in IST. Such records shall be retained for a period of at least twelve (12) months from the date of the relevant event. Customer may request access to such records in connection with a dispute regarding the calculation of any deadline or Service Level; Provider shall provide such access within five (5) Business Days of the request.

7.10 Customer Obligations. Customer shall ensure that any system or tool used to submit Support Requests or to generate timestamps that are relevant to this Agreement is configured to record time in IST, or that the time zone of such system or tool is clearly identified so that conversion to IST can be performed in accordance with Section 7.4. If Customer fails to comply with this Section 7.10, Provider may, in its sole discretion, rely on the timestamps generated by the Support Portal or by Provider's monitoring tools for purposes of measuring Service Levels.

8. SUPPORT SERVICES

8.1 Support Hours. Subject to the terms of this Agreement, Provider shall provide support services to Customer during the Support Hours. "Support Hours" means the hours from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM IST, Monday through Friday, excluding public holidays observed in the state of Karnataka. Support Hours shall not include any time on weekends or public holidays.

8.2 Severity Levels. Incidents shall be classified into the following severity levels, based on the impact on Customer's use of the Services:

(a) Severity 1 (Critical): A complete loss of a production service, or a material degradation of a production service that renders it unusable, with no workaround available.

8.3 Severity Level Assignment. Customer shall assign a severity level to each Incident at the time of submission, based on the definitions in Section 8.2 and the guidance in Exhibit C. If Customer does not assign a severity level, or assigns a level that Provider reasonably determines to be inconsistent with the definitions, Provider may reclassify the Incident and shall notify Customer of the reclassification within two (2) hours of such reclassification. Reclassification shall be effective from the time of the original submission for purposes of calculating response and resolution deadlines, provided Customer is notified in accordance with this Section 8.3.

8.4 Response and Resolution Deadlines. Provider shall respond to and resolve Incidents in accordance with the following deadlines, measured from the time of receipt of the Incident in the Support Portal:

(a) Severity 1: Initial response within thirty (30) minutes, continuous effort until resolution, and resolution or a workaround within four (4) hours.

(b) Severity 2: Initial response within two (2) hours, and resolution or a workaround within eight (8) Business Hours.

(c) Severity 3: Initial response within eight (8) Business Hours, and resolution or a workaround within three (3) Business Days.

(d) Severity 4: Initial response within two (2) Business Days, and resolution or a workaround within five (5) Business Days.

For purposes of this Section 8.4, "Business Hours" means the hours within Support Hours, and "Business Day" has the meaning set forth in Section 7.1. If an Incident is received outside Support Hours, the deadlines in this Section 8.4 shall commence at the start of the next Support Hours, except that for Severity 1 Incidents, Provider shall begin continuous effort immediately upon receipt regardless of Support Hours.

8.5 Escalation. Customer may escalate an Incident at any time by notifying the Provider's escalation contact identified in the Support Portal. Upon escalation, Provider shall assign a senior engineer or manager to the Incident and shall provide status updates at intervals of not more than sixty (60) minutes for Severity 1, or four (4) hours for all other severities, until the Incident is resolved or a workaround is provided.

8.6 Incident Reports. For each Severity 1 Incident, Provider shall provide a written incident report within five (5) Business Days of resolution. The report shall include a root cause analysis, a timeline of events, and a list of corrective actions to prevent recurrence. For Severity 2 and Severity 3 Incidents, Provider shall provide a summary report upon Customer's request, within five (5) Business Days of the request.

8.7 Change Requests. Customer may submit Change Requests through the Support Portal. Provider shall acknowledge receipt of a Change Request within two (2) Business Hours during Support Hours. Provider shall provide an impact assessment and a proposed implementation schedule within three (3) Business Days of receipt. Unless otherwise agreed in writing, Provider shall implement approved Change Requests within ten (10) Business Days of approval. Change Requests that require a change to the Services or to this Agreement shall be governed by Section 14 (Amendments).

8.8 Scheduled Maintenance. Provider may perform scheduled maintenance during the maintenance window from 12:00 AM to 4:00 AM IST on Sundays, provided that Provider gives Customer at least seven (7) days' prior written notice. Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to minimize the duration and impact of scheduled maintenance. Scheduled maintenance shall not count as downtime for purposes of the Service Level targets in Exhibit A.

9. FEES AND PAYMENT

9. REPORTING, PERFORMANCE REVIEWS, AND AUDIT RIGHTS

9.1 Monthly Reports. Within five (5) Business Days after the end of each calendar month, Provider shall deliver to Customer a written report (the "Monthly Report") covering the preceding calendar month. The Monthly Report shall include: (a) a summary of all Incidents reported, including their severity, time to acknowledge, time to resolution, and current status; (b) a summary of all Change Requests submitted, approved, implemented, or rejected; (c) a summary of Scheduled Maintenance performed; and (d) a statement of measured Service Level performance against the targets in Exhibit A, including any Service Credits accrued or payable.

9.2 Quarterly Business Reviews. Provider shall conduct a quarterly business review (a "QBR") with Customer within fifteen (15) Business Days after the end of each calendar quarter. The QBR may be held by video conference unless Customer requests an in-person meeting. The agenda for each QBR shall include: (a) a review of the Monthly Reports for the quarter; (b) a review of any Severity 1 Incidents and their corrective actions; (c) an assessment of Incidents and Change Requests by category and root cause; (d) a forward-looking capacity and demand plan; and (e) any other operational matters either party reasonably requests. Provider shall circulate an agenda at least five (5) Business Days before the QBR and shall circulate draft minutes within five (5) Business Days after the QBR. Customer shall provide comments on the draft minutes within five (5) Business Days of receipt, and the minutes shall be deemed final if no comments are received within that period.

9.3 Annual Performance Review. Within thirty (30) days after the end of each Agreement Year, Provider shall prepare and deliver to Customer a written annual performance summary covering: (a) aggregate performance against the Service Level targets in Exhibit A; (b) a consolidated root cause analysis of all Severity 1 Incidents; (c) an analysis of recurring Incident patterns and recommendations for improvement; (d) a summary of all Change Requests and their implementation outcomes; and (e) a capacity and performance outlook for the upcoming year. Provider shall present the annual performance summary at a meeting with Customer within fifteen (15) Business Days after delivery.

9.4 Audit Rights. Upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice, and no more than once per calendar year, Customer or its independent third-party auditor (which shall be bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than those in Section 12) may audit Provider's records and systems relating to the provision of the Services, including: (a) records of Incident response and resolution; (b) records of Change Request processing; (c) records of Scheduled Maintenance; (d) records of Service Level performance and Service Credits; and (e) records relating to Provider's compliance with its security and data protection obligations under Section 11. The audit shall be conducted during normal business hours at Provider's facilities and shall not unreasonably disrupt Provider's operations. Customer shall bear the cost of the audit unless the audit reveals a material breach of this Agreement or a material misstatement in any Monthly Report, in which case Provider shall reimburse Customer for the reasonable cost of the audit. Provider shall make available all relevant records within ten (10) Business Days of the audit commencement date and shall cooperate reasonably with the audit. Provider shall correct any deficiencies identified in the audit within thirty (30) days of the delivery of the audit report, or such other period as the parties may agree in writing.

10.1 **Initial Term.** This Agreement shall commence on 1 July 2024 (the "Effective Date") and shall continue in full force and effect for an initial term of twelve (12) months, expiring on 30 June 2025 (the "Initial Term"), unless earlier terminated in accordance with this Section 10.

Any termination for convenience shall not relieve Customer of its obligation to pay all fees due and payable for Services rendered prior to the effective date of termination, including any non-cancellable commitments for the remainder of the then-current Term.

(b) becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, files or has filed against it a petition in bankruptcy, or a receiver is appointed for a substantial part of its assets.

**14. DISPUTE RESOLUTION**

14.1 **Governing Law.** This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of India, without regard to its conflict of laws principles. The Parties expressly exclude the application of the United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods to this Agreement. Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Bengaluru, Karnataka, for any matter arising out of or relating to this Agreement, except as otherwise provided in this Section 14.

14.2 **Dispute Escalation.** Before either Party commences any arbitration or judicial proceeding (other than a proceeding seeking emergency injunctive or equitable relief), the Parties shall attempt in good faith to resolve any Dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement through the following escalation procedure:

(a) The claiming Party shall deliver a written Dispute Notice to the other Party, describing the Dispute in reasonable detail and identifying the individual authorised to represent the claiming Party in the resolution process;

(b) Within ten (10) Business Days of receipt of the Dispute Notice, the receiving Party shall designate an individual with authority to resolve the Dispute on its behalf and shall notify the claiming Party of that designation;

(c) The designated representatives shall meet (in person or by video conference) within fifteen (15) Business Days of the designation in an effort to resolve the Dispute amicably; and

(d) If the Dispute is not resolved within thirty (30) days of the initial Dispute Notice, either Party may proceed to arbitration in accordance with Section 14.3.

14.3 **Arbitration.** Any Dispute that is not resolved through the escalation procedure set forth in Section 14.2 shall be finally resolved by binding arbitration administered by the Bengaluru International Arbitration Centre (BIAC) in accordance with its Arbitration and Conciliation Rules in effect at the time of the arbitration, except as modified by this Agreement. The arbitration shall be conducted by a sole arbitrator appointed in accordance with the BIAC Rules. The seat and venue of the arbitration shall be Bengaluru, Karnataka, India, and the language of the arbitration shall be English.

(a) The arbitrator shall have the power to award any remedy or relief that a court of competent jurisdiction in India could order, including injunctive relief and specific performance, and shall issue a reasoned written award.

(b) The award of the arbitrator shall be final and binding upon the Parties, and judgment upon the award may be entered in any court having jurisdiction thereof. Each Party irrevocably waives any right to appeal the award except as provided under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

(c) Unless otherwise agreed by the Parties, the arbitration proceedings, including any pleadings, evidence, and the award, shall be kept confidential, and the Parties shall not disclose the existence or outcome of the arbitration to any third party, except as required by law or to enforce the award.

(d) The fees and costs of the arbitrator and the administrative fees of BIAC shall be borne as determined by the arbitrator, who may allocate such costs between the Parties in the award.

14.4 **Interim Relief.** Notwithstanding Section 14.3, either Party may seek interim or conservatory measures from a court of competent jurisdiction in Bengaluru, Karnataka, or from the arbitrator, as applicable, to protect its rights or property pending the resolution of the Dispute. The Parties agree that the exercise of such rights shall not constitute a waiver of the obligation to arbitrate.

EXHIBIT A — SERVICE CREDITS AND SLA REMEDIES

A.1 General. This Exhibit A sets forth the service credits and other remedies available to Customer in the event Asterion fails to meet the Service Levels defined in Section 4 of this Agreement. The remedies described in this Exhibit A are Customer’s sole and exclusive remedies for any failure to meet a Service Level, except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement.

A.2 Definitions. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Exhibit A shall have the meanings ascribed to them in Section 1 of this Agreement. For purposes of this Exhibit A:

(a) “Monthly Uptime Percentage” means the total number of minutes in a calendar month during which the applicable Service is available, minus any Excused Downtime, divided by the total number of minutes in that calendar month, expressed as a percentage.

(b) “Excused Downtime” means (i) Scheduled Maintenance, (ii) any downtime caused by factors outside Asterion’s reasonable control, including force majeure events as defined in Section 15.6, (iii) any downtime resulting from Customer’s or its users’ acts or omissions, including failure to comply with the Documentation or the Acceptable Use Policy, (iv) any downtime resulting from Customer’s hardware, software, network, or third-party services, or (v) any downtime caused by Customer’s failure to provide required access, information, or resources to Asterion.

(c) “Service Credit” means a credit against the Fees that Customer would otherwise be obligated to pay for the affected Service for the applicable calendar month, calculated in accordance with the table in Section A.3 below.

A.3 Service Credit Schedule. Service Credits shall be calculated based on the Monthly Uptime Percentage for the affected Service, as follows:

Monthly Uptime Percentage        Service Credit (% of Monthly Fee for the affected Service)
================================ ================================================================
Less than 99.9% but at least 99.5%   10%
Less than 99.5% but at least 99.0%   20%
Less than 99.0%                      30%

(a) Service Credits shall be applied to the invoice for the calendar month following the month in which the Service Level failure occurred. If no further invoice is expected, Asterion shall pay the Service Credit amount to Customer within thirty (30) days of issuance of the credit memo.

(b) Service Credits shall not be transferable or redeemable for cash, and shall not be applied to any Fees for Services other than the affected Service, unless the Parties agree otherwise in writing.

(c) Customer’s sole remedy for a failure to meet the Monthly Uptime Percentage shall be the Service Credits described in this Section A.3. Total Service Credits in any calendar month shall not exceed thirty percent (30%) of the monthly Fees for the affected Service.

A.4 Service Credit Claims. To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written claim to Asterion within thirty (30) days after the end of the calendar month in which the Service Level failure occurred. The claim must include: (a) the dates and times of the alleged Service Level failure, (b) a description of the impact on Customer’s use of the Service, and (c) any supporting documentation, such as monitoring reports or incident records. Asterion will review each claim in good faith and respond within fifteen (15) business days of receipt. If Asterion disputes the claim, the Parties shall follow the escalation procedure in Section 14.2. Failure to submit a timely claim shall waive Customer’s right to the Service Credit for that calendar month.

A.5 Scheduled Maintenance. Scheduled Maintenance shall be performed during the maintenance windows identified in the Documentation, which shall be at least eight (8) hours in duration and shall occur no more than once per calendar week, unless urgent maintenance is required to protect the security or integrity of the Service. Asterion shall provide at least seventy-two (72) hours’ advance notice of Scheduled Maintenance by email to the Customer’s designated technical contact. Scheduled Maintenance performed in accordance with this Section A.5 shall not count toward Excused Downtime or any Service Level calculation.
